facts.raw_span: a 4-month history of severe occipital and temporal headaches
headaches that were paroxysmal, aggravated by changes in position
associated with bilateral blurry vision and morning projectile vomiting
a kinetic and static cerebellar syndrome with ataxia, imbalance, uncoordinated movements, bilateral nystagmus, and stage I bilateral papilledema
Routine blood tests were unremarkable
Noncontrast CT of the head showed no abnormalities
an inferior median oval lesion of the cerebellar vermis measuring 40 × 31 × 29 mm
hypointense on T1-weighted images, heterogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted images
heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration
the lesion filled the foramen of Magendie, exerted mass effect on the medulla
no surrounding edema on FLAIR
elevated choline peak and reduced N-acetyl aspartate signal

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a large cerebellar lesion with heterogeneous enhancement and mass effect, are consistent with a medulloblastoma.
The patient's cerebellar lesion with heterogeneous enhancement and no surrounding edema could be consistent with a hemangioblastoma.
The patient's cerebellar syndrome and ataxia could be consistent with ataxia-telangiectasia, although the imaging findings are not typical.
The patient's cerebellar lesion with heterogeneous enhancement could be consistent with an astrocytoma.
The patient's cerebellar syndrome and mass effect on the medulla could be consistent with a brainstem glioma.
The patient's cerebellar lesion with heterogeneous enhancement could be consistent with a metastasis, although there is no known primary tumor.
The patient's cerebellar lesion with heterogeneous enhancement could be consistent with an ependymoma.
The patient's cerebellar lesion with heterogeneous enhancement could be consistent with a ganglioglioma.

rationales.F09: The enhancement pattern is consistent with a cerebellar tumor.
rationales.F10: The mass effect and location of the lesion are consistent with a cerebellar tumor.
rationales.F12: The spectroscopy findings are consistent with a cerebellar tumor.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with a cerebellar syndrome, including ataxia, imbalance, and nystagmus, along with the MRI findings of a cerebellar vermis lesion with heterogeneous enhancement, is more consistent with a Cerebellar Astrocytoma, which is a common cerebellar tumor in adults.
